purpose: Teach: やっこ/一足/脅かす/隔て/嫌気/愉し/溜め/好転

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、夏の冷ややっこをお父さんが好まれた
lines.en: Gran, when I was young — Dad loved cold tofu in summer.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle pause after 'Gran' — gathering a memory. Quiet, reflective pace. Voice trails slightly into the specific detail, as if seeing it again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、人より一足早く起きてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, Grandpa — he used to wake up before everyone else, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm affirmation with a knowing lilt. Gentle reminder in her tone, not a correction. The 'dear' is unspoken but present. Soft, encouraging cadence that invites him to keep remembering.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは子供を脅かす遊びを嫌がられた
lines.en: Gran, when I was young — Dad hated games where you'd startle the children.
lines.style: Same wistful opening. Measured delivery of this smaller detail. Voice holds the observation gently, as if it's precious precisely because it's small and true.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦中、家族と距離を隔てて暮らされた時期があったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa — during the war, there was a time your family lived apart. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Tender but direct. No sugar-coating the difficult memory. Her voice steadies as she names it. A gentle prompt — she's asking him to hold this too, together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは仕事に嫌気を見せず勤勉だった
lines.en: Gran, when I was young — Dad showed up to work every single day, never complained.
lines.style: Quiet admiration in the phrasing. Slow, deliberate. The words land with the weight of understanding what that steadiness cost and meant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、孫との会話を愉しいと仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa — you used to say talking with the grandchildren made you happy. I remember you saying that.
lines.style: Warmth with a gentle tease underneath. Soft assertion — she's reminding him of something good he believed. Closes with tenderness, no trailing off, grounded.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがコツコツと貯金を溜められた
lines.en: Gran, when I was young — Dad saved money, bit by bit, year after year.
lines.style: Slow, deliberate. Voice gathers weight with each phrase — the accumulation matters. Quiet respect in the delivery. Slight breath before the final image settles.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦後、暮らしが好転した日々を喜ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa — after the war, when things finally began to get better, you were so glad. I saw that in you.
lines.style: Tender and certain. No question mark in her voice, even though the sentence curves upward. She's witnessed his joy and is naming it back to him with love. Gentle close, present tense underneath.
